This studies target the Excees Return of amercian politician, the goal is to analyse the relationship of excess return and net gain beetween party, state and politician.

  1. Trade Size and number

We are now Considering the size and the number of trade per year and per month and trying to compute some correlation beetween it.

The mid size of trade per year presented as follow :

## years
## 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 
## 3205 3797 3786 4087 4394 5377 7699 5377 3652 4383  710

It is interesting to asses if there is some correlation between the size of the trade per month and the number of trade. Here is a plot of both of them to compare visualy.

The plot let us a doubt about the corraltion, Based on the analysis, the Spearman correlation between the number of trades per month and trade size per month is 0.6032014 and the Pearson is0.4444545 , indicating a strong positive relationship.

There is a seriously correlation between the trade size per month and the trade number per month, This is logical because it mean that the size of trade are quite balance. We can see it with a plot of linear trend.

Let’s now see if there is any correlation beetween number of trade and month or year.

The correlation spearman per year is 0.0911164 and per month is -0.0642355 , This mean that there is no correlation

This graph show that this is quite stable and that the number of trade do not depend on the months, We can also compute the same for the trade size.The average trade size is 4.1135234^{4}

Let see what happened stastically with excess return :

summary(df$excess_return)
##     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max.     NA's 
##  -318.75   -84.40   -27.71   -15.03    16.10 10885.41     2506

The results are very negative which is not normal. this is because A lot of NA’s messing with the numbers biased the result, lets ignore them :

The mean will be now : -15.0291822 The median will be : -27.7138947 the standars deviation : 179.90644

Interpretation

On average, trades underperformed the market benchmark by ~15%. This is slightly higher than the median because a few very large positive trades pull the mean up.

More than half of all trades underperformed the benchmark by ~28%. This confirms a negative skew: most trades lost relative to the market.

Extremely high variability → trade outcomes are very volatile. extreme outliers like 10,885 or −318 heavily influence dispersion.

##1. Histogram of trade size

#LOG scale

ggplot(df, aes(x = trade_size_mid)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = “steelblue”, color = “white”) + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) + labs( title = “Distribution of Trade Size (Log Scale)”, x = “Trade Size (USD, log10)”, y = “Count” ) + theme_minimal()

#categorising trade size

df <- df %>% mutate(trade_size_cat = case_when( trade_size_mid < 1e4 ~ “< $10k”, trade_size_mid < 5e4 ~ “$10k–$50k”, trade_size_mid < 1e5 ~ “$50k–$100k”, trade_size_mid < 5e5 ~ “$100k–$500k”, TRUE ~ “> $500k” ))

ggplot(df, aes(x = trade_size_cat)) + geom_bar(fill = “steelblue”) + labs( title = “Trade Size Categories”, x = “Trade Size Category”, y = “Number of Trades” ) + theme_minimal()

##2. Boxplot: excess return by party

ggplot(df, aes(x = Party, y = excess_return)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-300, 300)) + labs( title = “Excess Return by Party”, x = “Party”, y = “Excess Return” ) + theme_minimal()

##3.1 Boxplot: excess return by chamber

ggplot(df, aes(x = Chamber, y = excess_return)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-300, 300)) + labs( title = “Excess Return by Chamber”, x = “Chamber”, y = “Excess Return” ) + theme_minimal()

##3.2 excess return by state/ net gain by state

ggplot(df, aes(x = State, y = excess_return)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-300, 300)) + labs( title = “Excess Return by State”, x = “State”, y = “Excess Return” ) + theme_minimal()

state_means <- df %>% group_by(State) %>% summarise(mean_excess_return = mean(excess_return, na.rm = TRUE))

state_means2 <- df %>% group_by(State) %>% summarise(net_gain = mean(net_gain, na.rm = TRUE))

us_states <- map_data(“state”)

state_means <- state_means %>% mutate(State = tolower(State))

state_means2 <- state_means2 %>% mutate(State = tolower(State))

map_df <- left_join( us_states, state_means, by = c(“region” = “State”) )

ggplot(map_df, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = mean_excess_return)) + geom_polygon(color = “white”, linewidth = 0.2) + coord_fixed(1.3) + scale_fill_gradient2( low = “red”, mid = “white”, high = “blue”, midpoint = 0, na.value = “grey90” ) + labs( title = “Mean Excess Return by State”, fill = “Mean Excess Return” ) + theme_void()

map_df2 <- left_join( us_states, state_means2, by = c(“region” = “State”) )

ggplot(map_df2, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = net_gain)) + geom_polygon(color = “white”, linewidth = 0.2) + coord_fixed(1.3) + scale_fill_gradient2( low = “blue”, mid = “white”, high = “red”, midpoint = 0, na.value = “grey90” ) + labs( title = “net gain by state”, fill = “Mean net gain” ) + theme_void()

##3.3 Boxplot: excess return by party

ggplot(df, aes(x = Party, y = excess_return)) + geom_point(na.rm = TRUE)+ geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-300, 300)) + labs( title = “Excess Return by Party”, x = “Party”, y = “Excess Return” ) + theme_minimal()

##4. Boxplot: excess return by transaction type

ggplot(df, aes(x = Transaction, y = excess_return)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-300, 300)) + labs( title = “Excess Return by Transaction Type”, x = “Transaction Type”, y = “Excess Return” ) + theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

##6. Clean time series: number of trades over time

df_ts <- df %>% mutate(Month = as.Date(paste0(format(Traded, “%Y-%m”), “-01”))) %>% group_by(Month) %>% summarise(num_trades = n(), .groups = “drop”)

ggplot(df_ts, aes(x = Month, y = num_trades)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + labs( title = “Number of Trades Over Time (Monthly)”, x = “Month”, y = “Number of Trades” ) + theme_minimal()
